package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via phishing email, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: GermanWiper is a destructive ransomware variant that, instead of encrypting files, irreversibly deletes them while misleading victims into believing that paying a ransom will restore their data. This behavior is intentionally deceptive and destructive, causing permanent data loss.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after user opens malicious attachment from phishing email)
execution_context.file_location: malicious executable delivered via email attachment

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: for each file in user directories: overwrite file content with random data; delete file; display ransom note.
malicious_snippets.code_language: windows executable (likely C/C++ or Delphi, but not specified)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code iterates through user files, overwrites their contents with random data, deletes the files, and then displays a ransom note to the victim, falsely claiming files can be restored upon payment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code irreversibly destroys user data while pretending to be ransomware, which is both destructive and deceptive.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal ransomware encrypts files and may restore them after payment; this code deletes files permanently, violating user trust and expectations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Secure file deletion tools may overwrite and delete files, but only with explicit user consent and not as part of a phishing attack.
key_indicators: Display of ransom note despite no possibility of recovery
Execution triggered by opening a phishing email attachment

attack_chain.action: Victim receives and opens a phishing email with a malicious attachment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the GermanWiper malware payload

attack_chain.action: Malware executes, iterates through user files, overwrites and deletes them.
Ransom note is displayed, misleading the victim into believing files can be recovered by paying.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential ransom payment with no possibility of data recovery

behavioral_signatures: Mass file overwriting and deletion in rapid succession
Display of ransom note after file destruction
Execution of unknown binaries delivered via email attachments
file_indicators: Presence of ransom note files (e.g., README.txt, DECRYPT_INSTRUCTIONS.txt)
Unusual deletion of user files in common directories (Documents, Desktop, etc.)
network_indicators: No significant network activity required for file destruction, but may attempt to contact C2 or payment instructions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for processes that rapidly overwrite and delete large numbers of user files, especially following the execution of email attachments. Look for the creation of ransom note files and alert on mass file deletion events. Endpoint protection should block unknown executables delivered via email and flag behaviors matching destructive ransomware patterns.
